title: Mechanistic study on ligustilide modulation of the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway in ameliorating Scopolamine-Induced cognitive impairment.
authors: Zhang, Qian; Gao, Minghuang; Xu, Ziqiao; Xu, Jiaqi; Zhong, Guangcheng; Yang, Hongying; Yang, Cong; Wang, Qi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药藁本内酯通过TLR4/NF-κB通路改善认知障碍，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: This research employed a multi-method strategy integrating network pharmacology, molecular docking, and animal experiments to investigate the therapeutic mechanisms of ligustilide in Alzheimer's disease (AD) management. AD-related targets were obtained from GeneCards, while ligustilide-associated targets were identified using SwissTargetPrediction. Protein interaction networks were constructed via the STRING database. Functional annotation and pathway enrichment analysis were performed using Metascape, including Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses revealing that ligustilide modulated AD progression primarily by regulating the Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor kappa B (TLR4/NF-kappaB) signaling pathway. Molecular docking studies conducted with AutoDock Vina demonstrated strong binding affinities between ligustilide and key targets in this pathway. Behavioral evaluations, including locomotor activity assessment (open field test), spatial memory analysis (Morris water maze), and recognition memory testing (novel object recognition test) demonstrated that ligustilide significantly attenuated SCOP-induced cognitive deficits. Histopathological and biochemical analyses indicated that ligustilide maintained cholinergic neuron integrity and boosted antioxidant defenses in SCOP-treated mice. Transcriptional profiling revealed decreased expression of TLR4, NF-kappaB p65, and pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6) in ligustilide-treated AD model mice. Western blot and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) demonstrated reduced levels of TLR4, phosphorylated p65 (Ser536), TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IL-6 in ligustilide-treated AD model mice. These findings collectively demonstrate that ligustilide alleviates SCOP-induced cognitive deficits through suppression of the TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling cascade.
abstract_zh: 本研究采用网络药理学、分子对接与动物实验相结合的多方法策略，探讨藁本内酯（ligustilide）在阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）治疗中的机制。AD相关靶点从GeneCards获取，而藁本内酯相关靶点通过SwissTargetPrediction鉴定。蛋白相互作用网络通过STRING数据库构建。功能注释和通路富集分析使用Metascape进行，包括基因本体论（Gene Ontology）和KEGG通路分析，结果显示藁本内酯主要通过调节Toll样受体4/核因子kappa B（TLR4/NF-kappaB）信号通路来调控AD进展。使用AutoDock Vina进行的分子对接研究表明，藁本内酯与该通路中关键靶点具有强结合亲和力。行为学评估，包括运动活性评估（旷场试验）、空间记忆分析（Morris水迷宫）和识别记忆测试（新物体识别试验），表明藁本内酯显著减轻了SCOP诱导的认知缺陷。组织病理学和生化分析表明，藁本内酯在SCOP处理的小鼠中维持了胆碱能神经元完整性并增强了抗氧化防御能力。转录谱分析显示，在藁本内酯处理的AD模型小鼠中，TLR4、NF-kappaB p65及促炎介质（TNF-alpha、IL-1beta、IL-6）的表达降低。Western blot和酶联免疫吸附试验（ELISA）显示，在藁本内酯处理的AD模型小鼠中，TLR4、磷酸化p65（Ser536）、TNF-alpha、IL-1beta和IL-6水平降低。这些发现共同表明，藁本内酯通过抑制TLR4/NF-kappaB信号级联反应来缓解SCOP诱导的认知缺陷。
